## Design

### 2026-10-21 – I worked a ton on a massive schematic. I added an ESP32 S3 to control everything and then added a ton of connectors, resistors, power controlling circuits with polarized and non polarized capacitors,

**4h**

I worked a ton on a massive schematic. I added an ESP32 S3 to control everything and then added a ton of connectors, resistors, power controlling circuits with polarized and non polarized capacitors, resistors, fuses, push buttons, potentiometers, and plenty of more stuff. This is going to be the noise and music for the arm so I made it thoroughly. I haven't figured out the way it connects to the PI yet though and I left a ton of pins for if I might need it later. Making the resistor bridges was definitely the hardest part, especially since the ERC kept flagging it.

### 2026-10-21 – I swapped the 3.3V regulator for a R-78B3.3 for safer voltage control and ease to solder, I added an ESD chip for the safety of the USB-C, I added no-connect markers to everything, fine-tuned the ERC,

**6h**

I swapped the 3.3V regulator for a R-78B3.3 for safer voltage control and ease to solder, I added an ESD chip for the safety of the USB-C, I added no-connect markers to everything, fine-tuned the ERC, added a ton of more resistors for safety, resistor bridges, a few diodes, added footprints to everything, and now I think it's ready for making into an actual PCB.  I worked so much on this and I'm so tired now. I'm just glad I can have this funding and be able to learn and work on this. FYI I accidentally added this to week 1 and there was no way to reverse it that I could find easily so I'm sorry. That was an accident.

### 2026-10-23 – I tried working on the massive amount of errors but nothing worked. I tried moving the parts, I tried re-routing it so many times, and I tried so many different techniques but nothing worked. As a res

**6h**

I tried working on the massive amount of errors but nothing worked. I tried moving the parts, I tried re-routing it so many times, and I tried so many different techniques but nothing worked. As a result, I decided the best course of action was to redo it all. I feel like it was overkill - a separate esp32 just for a speaker? And a microphone? That was way too much. I redid it all and made a way simpler V2 - just a headphone jack, capacitors, and a few more connectors for the modules like the speaker. It's way simpler and I was able to make it pretty fast surprisingly. There's still a few more things that need to be verified, but other than that I think it's ready.
